headline: Underwriting strength lifts profit as catastrophes ease
summary_short: Allstate's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 11.8% y/y to $18.596 billion on policy growth and higher homeowners pricing, while net income climbed 55.1% y/y to $3.271 billion as the Property-Liability combined ratio improved to 86.6 from 91.1.
summary_long: Revenue grew 11.8% y/y to $18.596 billion on higher policies in force, increased homeowners insurance pricing, and strong investment results. Property-Liability underwriting income more than doubled to $2.006 billion as the combined ratio improved 4.5 points to 86.6, aided by lower catastrophe losses ($1.722B vs $1.990B) and favorable prior-year reserve releases, partly offset by higher legal expenses. Net investment income rose to $1.009 billion on higher fixed-income yields and performance-based gains. Net income rose 55.1% y/y to $3.271 billion; diluted EPS was $12.51 (+61.2% y/y). Allstate repurchased $1.0 billion of stock and paid $280 million in dividends. Shareholders' equity rose to $33.698 billion. The release issued no new forward guidance.

drivers.explanation: Growth reflects increased policies in force, higher average homeowners insurance premiums, and strong investment results, per management's quarter summary.
Growth is attributed to strong underwriting results -- Property-Liability underwriting income more than doubled y/y on lower catastrophe losses and favorable reserve releases.
Rise tracks the $1.439B y/y improvement in pretax income before tax, itself driven by lower catastrophe losses and higher Property-Liability underwriting income.
Growth reflects retained-income accumulation from strong net income, partially offset by treasury-stock buybacks and dividends paid during the period.
Diluted share count fell as this quarter's $1.0 billion of buybacks reduced common shares outstanding to 253.5 million from 263.8 million a year earlier.
Management called the quarter's operating and financial results "excellent," citing Transformative Growth execution and $3.5 billion of trailing-twelve-month shareholder returns (6.7% of market cap).
